stops.name: The wilderness, Korah swallowed by the earth
stops.campa: Korah of the Levites, with Dathan and Abiram and two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, rises against Moses and Aaron: "ye take too much upon you." Moses bids each bring his censer, and let the LORD show whom He has chosen. He warns the congregation to depart from the tents of these wicked men. As he ends speaking, the ground cleaves asunder; the earth opens her mouth and swallows Korah's men and their houses and their goods, and they go down alive into the pit. Fire from the LORD consumes the two hundred and fifty who offered incense; their censers are beaten into plates for the altar.
stops.quote: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.

stops.name: Kadesh (Meribah), the striking of the rock; the sin that bars him
stops.campa: In the fortieth year the people come again to Kadesh, and there is no water, and they chide with Moses, wishing they had died with their brethren. God tells Moses to take the rod and speak to the rock before their eyes, that it give forth water. But Moses gathers them and cries, "Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?" and smites the rock twice with the rod. Water comes out abundantly, and the congregation drinks. Yet because he believed not, to sanctify God before Israel, the LORD says he shall not bring this congregation into the land. It is the waters of Meribah, strife.
stops.quote: Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.

stops.name: Mount Hor, the death of Aaron
stops.campa: Miriam dies at Kadesh and is buried there. Then, on the edge of Edom, at Mount Hor, the LORD tells Moses that Aaron shall be gathered to his people, for he too rebelled at Meribah. Before all the congregation Moses brings Aaron and his son Eleazar up the mount, and strips Aaron of his priestly garments and puts them upon Eleazar; and Aaron dies there on the top of the mount. Moses and Eleazar come down, and when all the congregation see that Aaron is dead, they mourn for him thirty days, all the house of Israel. The office passes; the brother is gone.
stops.quote: And Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah.

stops.name: The way of the Red Sea, the fiery serpents and the bronze serpent
stops.campa: Compassing the land of Edom, the soul of the people is much discouraged, and they speak against God and Moses: "there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread." The LORD sends fiery serpents among them, and much people of Israel die. They repent and come to Moses, who prays for them. The LORD says, Make thee a fiery serpent and set it upon a pole; every one that is bitten shall look upon it and live. So Moses makes a serpent of brass and sets it on a pole; and if a serpent bites any man, he looks and lives.
stops.quote: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.

stops.name: Beer, the Song of the Well
stops.campa: Passing the brooks of Arnon and the border of the Amorites, Israel comes to Beer, the well; that is the well whereof the LORD spake to Moses, Gather the people, and I will give them water. Then Israel sings this song, a joy after so much murmuring: "Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it." The nobles and princes of the people dig it with the lawgiver's staff. From the wilderness they journey on to Mattanah, and Nahaliel, and Bamoth, and to the valley in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks toward Jeshimon.
stops.quote: Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it.

stops.name: The valley of Pethor, Balaam and the speaking donkey
stops.campa: Balak king of Moab, dreading Israel encamped in his plains, sends for Balaam the seer to curse them. Balaam saddles his donkey and rides; the angel of the LORD stands in the way with a drawn sword, unseen by the prophet but seen by the beast. Three times the donkey turns aside, and Balaam smites her; then the LORD opens the donkey's mouth, and she says, "What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?" Balaam's eyes are opened; he sees the angel and falls flat. Brought to the high places, he can only bless: "How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob!"
stops.quote: And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?

stops.name: The plains of Moab by Jordan, the words of Deuteronomy
stops.campa: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, in the fortieth year, the eleventh month, Moses begins to declare the law. He rehearses the whole journey from Horeb, the giving of the commandments, the wandering; he pleads with the new generation to love the LORD, to keep His statutes, to choose life. He recites the great Shema: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD." He sets before them blessing and cursing, life and death, and sings his song of witness, and blesses the twelve tribes each by name, as a father over his children before he goes.
stops.quote: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: and thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.

stops.name: Mount Nebo, the top of Pisgah: the sight of the whole Land
stops.campa: Moses goes up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. And the LORD shows him all the land: Gilead unto Dan, all Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, all Judah unto the utmost sea, the south, and the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, unto Zoar. This is the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, given to their seed: he is caused to see it with his eyes, but shall not go over thither. A hundred and twenty years old, his eye not dim, his force not abated, he looks upon the promise he may not enter.
stops.quote: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.

stops.name: The valley over against Beth-peor: no man knoweth his sepulchre
stops.campa: So Moses the servant of the LORD dies there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD. The aggadah tells it was by the kiss of God, His breath drawing forth the soul of the faithful shepherd. And God Himself buries him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth-peor; but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. The children of Israel weep for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days. There arises not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face. Joshua takes up the mantle; the people go over Jordan without him.
stops.quote: And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth-peor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
